chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
I swear by Him Who let us pass the dark night after which there was a bright day that such and such [1] did not happen.

key_terms.غُبْرِ: dust or haze, referring to the darkness or obscurity of the night
key_terms.كَذَا وَكَذَا: such and such (indicating a specific, previously mentioned event)

ai.seo_question: What does the metaphor of the dark night and bright day signify in this oath of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this eloquent oath from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali employs the vivid imagery of a 'dark, cloudy night' giving way to a 'bright, clear day' to emphasize the certainty and clarity of the truth he is asserting. This rhetorical device, characteristic of classical Arabic eloquence, underscores the transition from obscurity to illumination, reinforcing the divine authority behind his words. The phrase highlights the Imam's role as a guide who dispels doubt through the light of divine truth.
